A BIM is a shared knowledge resource for information about a facility forming a reliable basis for decisions during its life-cycle; defined as existing from earliest conception to demolition.''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nationalbimstandard.org/faq.php#faq1 |title=Frequently Asked Questions About the National BIM Standard-United States – National BIM Standard – United States |publisher=Nationalbimstandard.org |access-date=17 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016190503/http://www.nationalbimstandard.org/faq.php#faq1 |archive-date=16 October 2014 }}</ref>

Traditional building design was largely reliant upon two-dimensional [[technical drawings]] (plans, elevations, sections, etc.). Building information modeling extends the three primary spatial dimensions (width, height and depth), incorporating information about time (so-called 4D BIM),<ref name=4DBIM-R-01 /> cost (5D BIM),<ref name="5DBIM-R-02" /> asset management, sustainability, etc. BIM therefore covers more than just geometry. It also covers spatial relationships, geospatial information, quantities and properties of building components (for example, manufacturers' details), and enables a wide range of collaborative processes relating to the built asset from initial planning through to construction and then throughout its operational life.

BIM authoring tools present a design as combinations of "objects" – vague and undefined, generic or product-specific, solid shapes or void-space oriented (like the shape of a room), that carry their geometry, relations, and attributes. BIM applications allow extraction of different views from a building model for drawing production and other uses. These different views are automatically consistent, being based on a single definition of each object instance.<ref name = "Eastman, C">{{cite web |last=Eastman |first=Chuck |date=August 2009 |title=What is BIM? |url=http://bim.arch.gatech.edu/?id=402 |access-date=24 January 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191026115715/http://bim.arch.gatech.edu/?id=402 |archive-date=26 October 2019 }}</ref> BIM software also defines objects parametrically; that is, the objects are defined as parameters and relations to other objects so that if a related object is amended, dependent ones will automatically also change.<ref name = "Eastman, C"/> Each model element can carry attributes for selecting and ordering them automatically, providing cost estimates as well as material tracking and ordering.<ref name = "Eastman, C"/>

For the professionals involved in a project, BIM enables a virtual information model to be shared by the design team ([[architect]]s, [[landscape architect]]s, [[surveying|surveyor]]s, [[civil engineering|civil]], [[structural engineering|structural]] and [[building services]] [[engineer]]s, etc.), [[general contractor|main contractor]], [[subcontractor]]s and the owner/operator. Each professional adds discipline-specific data to the shared model – commonly, a 'federated' model which combines several different disciplines' models into one.<ref name="McPartland-11Sep2017">{{cite news |last1=McPartland |first1=Richard |title=What is a federated Building Information Model? |url=https://www.thenbs.com/knowledge/what-is-a-federated-building-information-model |access-date=26 May 2020 |work=NBS: Knowledge |publisher=NBS |date=11 September 2017 |archive-date=15 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915082837/https://www.thenbs.com/knowledge/what-is-a-federated-building-information-model |url-status=live }}</ref> Combining models enables visualisation of all models in a single environment, better coordination and development of designs, enhanced clash avoidance and detection, and improved time and cost decision-making.<ref name="McPartland-11Sep2017"/>

==='BIM wash'===
"BIM wash" or "BIM washing" is a term sometimes used to describe inflated, and/or deceptive, claims of using or delivering BIM services or products.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bimthinkspace.com/2011/06/episode-16-understanding-bim-wash.html|title=Understanding BIM Wash|date=6 June 2011|publisher=BIM Thinkspace|access-date=25 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://buildinginformationmanagement.wordpress.com/2011/12/13/green-washing-and-cloud-washing-terms-you-must-know-relative-to-bim-not-to-mention-bim-washing/|title=Green-Washing and Cloud-Washing – Terms you must know relative to BIM – Not to mention BIM-Washing|date=12 December 2011|publisher=buildinginformationmanagement.wordpress.com|access-date=25 February 2012|archive-date=17 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217192913/http://buildinginformationmanagement.wordpress.com/2011/12/13/green-washing-and-cloud-washing-terms-you-must-know-relative-to-bim-not-to-mention-bim-washing/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Succar |first=Bilal |date=2011-06-05 |title=Episode 16: Understanding BIM Wash |url=https://bimexcellence.org/thinkspace/episode-16-understanding-bim-wash/ |access-date=2026-08-16 |website=BIMe Initiative |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Usage throughout the asset life cycle==
Use of BIM goes beyond the planning and design phase of a project, extending throughout the life cycle of the asset. The supporting processes of [[building lifecycle management]] include [[cost management]], [[construction management]], [[project management]], [[facilities management|facility operation]] and [[Building information modeling in green building|application in]] [[green building]].

===Common Data Environment===
A 'Common Data Environment' (CDE) is defined in ISO 19650 as an:

:''Agreed source of information for any given project or asset, for collecting, managing and disseminating each information container through a managed process.''<ref>ISO 19650-1:2018, p. 3.3.15.</ref>

A CDE workflow describes the processes to be used while a CDE solution can provide the underlying technologies. A CDE is used to share data across a project or asset lifecycle, supporting collaboration across a whole project team. The concept of a CDE overlaps with [[enterprise content management]], ECM, but with a greater focus on BIM issues.

===Management of building information models===
Building information models span the whole concept-to-occupation time-span. To ensure efficient management of information processes throughout this span, a BIM manager might be appointed. The BIM manager is retained by a design build team on the client's behalf from the pre-design phase onwards to develop and to track the object-oriented BIM against predicted and measured performance objectives, supporting multi-disciplinary building information models that drive analysis, schedules, take-off and logistics.<ref>[https://www.gsa.gov/Portal/gsa/ep/channelView.do?pageTypeId=17109&channelPage=/ep/channel/gsaOverview.jsp&channelId=-24291]   {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091112145341/http://www.gsa.gov/Portal/gsa/ep/channelView.do?pageTypeId=17109&channelPage=%2Fep%2Fchannel%2FgsaOverview.jsp&channelId=-24291|date=12 November 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.senaatti.fi/document.asp?siteID=2&docID=588|title=Senate Properties modeling guidelines|publisher=Gsa.gov|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120226194436/http://www.senaatti.fi/document.asp?siteID=2&docID=588|archive-date=26 February 2012}}</ref> BIMs were also developed to different levels of development (LOD) (sometimes also called [[Level of detail (computer graphics)|levels of detail]]) reflecting the relevant levels of detailing needed from early to later stages of a project.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.autcon.2010.11.027 |title=Analysis of modeling effort and impact of different levels of detail in building information models |year=2011 |last1=Leite |first1=Fernanda |last2=Akcamete |first2=Asli |last3=Akinci |first3=Burcu |last4=Atasoy |first4=Guzide |last5=Kiziltas |first5=Semiha |journal=[[Automation in Construction]] |volume=20 |issue=5 |pages=601–9|hdl=11511/35062 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> The 2018 publication of ISO 19650-1 then introduced the concept of Level of Information Need (LOIN), standardised in 2024 in ISO 7817-1:2024.<ref>''[https://www.iso.org/standard/82914.html ISO 7817-1:2024 Building information modelling — Level of information need, Part 1: Concepts and principles]''. ISO. Retrieved 11 June 2026</ref>

===BIM in construction management===
Participants in the building process are constantly challenged to deliver successful projects despite tight budgets, limited staffing, accelerated schedules, and limited or conflicting information. The significant disciplines such as [[Architectural engineering|architectural]], [[Structural engineering|structural]] and [[mechanical, electrical, and plumbing|MEP]] designs should be well-coordinated, as two things can't take place at the same place and time. BIM additionally is able to aid in collision detection, identifying the exact location of discrepancies.  
   
The BIM concept envisages virtual construction of a facility prior to its actual physical construction, in order to reduce uncertainty, improve safety, work out problems, and simulate and analyze potential impacts.<ref name = "Smith 2007">{{cite journal |first1=Deke |last1=Smith |year=2007 |title=An Introduction to Building Information Modeling (BIM) |journal=Journal of Building Information Modeling |url=http://www.wbdg.org/pdfs/jbim_fall07.pdf |pages=12–4 |access-date=25 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013172534/http://wbdg.org/pdfs/jbim_fall07.pdf |archive-date=13 October 2011 }}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=January 2012}} Sub-contractors from every trade can input critical information into the model before beginning construction, with opportunities to pre-fabricate or pre-assemble some systems off-site. Waste can be minimised on-site and products delivered on a just-in-time basis rather than being stock-piled on-site.<ref name = "Smith 2007"/>

Quantities and shared properties of materials can be extracted easily. Scopes of work can be isolated and defined. Systems, assemblies and sequences can be shown in a relative scale with the entire facility or group of facilities. BIM also prevents errors by enabling conflict or 'clash detection' whereby the computer model visually highlights to the team where parts of the building (e.g.:structural frame and building services pipes or ducts) may wrongly intersect.

===BIM in facility operation and asset management===
BIM can bridge the information loss associated with handing a project from design team, to construction team and to building owner/operator, by allowing each group to add to and reference back to all information they acquire during their period of contribution to the BIM model. Enabling an effective handover of information from design and construction (including via IFC or COBie) can thus yield benefits to the facility owner or operator.<ref name="Kelly-25Apr2018">{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Graham |title=Back to Basics – The What, How and Why of BIM and FM |url=https://www.bimplus.co.uk/back-basics-what-how-and-why-bim-and-fm/ |access-date=8 January 2024 |work=BIM Plus |date=25 April 2018}}</ref> BIM-related processes relating to longer-term asset management are also covered in ISO-19650 Part 3.<ref name="GeoSp-23Jan2019"/>

For example, a building owner may find evidence of a water leak in a building. Rather than exploring the physical building, the owner may turn to the model and see that a water [[valve]] is located in the suspect location. The owner could also have in the model the specific valve size, manufacturer, part number, and any other information ever researched in the past, pending adequate computing power. Such problems were initially addressed by Leite and Akinci when developing a vulnerability representation of facility contents and threats for supporting the identification of vulnerabilities in building emergencies.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1061/(ASCE)CP.1943-5487.0000171 |title=Formalized Representation for Supporting Automated Identification of Critical Assets in Facilities during Emergencies Triggered by Failures in Building Systems |year=2012 |last1=Leite |first1=Fernanda |last2=Akinci |first2=Burcu |journal=Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering |volume=26 |issue=4 |page=519}}</ref>

[[File:Operational BIM 2D floor plan view in a mobile device.png|thumb|Operational BIM 2D floor plan view in a mobile device]]
Dynamic information about the building, such as sensor measurements and control signals from the building systems, can also be incorporated within software to support analysis of building operation and maintenance.<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1061/41052(346)10 |chapter=Requirements and Evaluation of Standards for Integration of Sensor Data with Building Information Models |title=Computing in Civil Engineering |year=2009 |last1=Liu |first1=Xuesong |last2=Akinci |first2=Burcu |isbn=978-0-7844-1052-3 |pages=95–104 |editor1-first=Carlos H. |editor1-last=Caldas |editor2-first=William J. |editor2-last=O'Brien}}</ref> As such, BIM in facility operation can be related to [[internet of things]] approaches;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tang |first1=Shu |last2=Shelden |first2=Dennis R. |last3=Eastman |first3=Charles M. |last4=Pishdad-Bozorgi |first4=Pardis |last5=Gao |first5=Xinghua |date=May 2019 |title=A review of building information modeling (BIM) and the internet of things (IoT) devices integration: Present status and future trends |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0926580518305764 |journal=Automation in Construction |language=en |volume=101 |pages=127–139 |doi=10.1016/j.autcon.2019.01.020 |bibcode=2019AutCo.101..127T |url-access=subscription }}</ref> rapid access to data may also be aided by use of mobile devices (smartphones, tablets) and machine-readable [[Radio-frequency identification|RFID]] tags or [[barcodes]];<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Costin |first1=Aaron M. |last2=Teizer |first2=Jochen |date=December 2015 |title=Fusing passive RFID and BIM for increased accuracy in indoor localization |journal=Visualization in Engineering |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |article-number=17 |doi=10.1186/s40327-015-0030-6 |doi-access=free |issn=2213-7459}}</ref> while integration and interoperability with other business systems - [[Computer-aided facility management|CAFM]], [[Enterprise resource planning|ERP]], [[Building automation|BMS]], IWMS, etc - can aid operational reuse of data.

There have been attempts at creating information models for older, pre-existing facilities. Approaches include referencing key metrics such as the [[Facility Condition Index]] (FCI), or using [[3D scanner|3D laser-scanning]] surveys and [[photogrammetry]] techniques (separately or in combination) or digitizing traditional building surveying methodologies by using mobile technology to capture accurate measurements and operation-related information about the asset that can be used as the basis for a model. Trying to retrospectively model a building constructed in, say 1927, requires numerous assumptions about design standards, building codes, construction methods, materials, etc, and is, therefore, more complex than building a model during design.

One of the challenges to the proper maintenance and management of existing facilities is understanding how BIM can be utilized to support a holistic understanding and implementation of [[Facility management|building management]] practices and "[[Total cost of ownership|cost of ownership]]" principles that support the full [[product lifecycle]] of a building. An [[American National Standards Institute|American National Standard]] entitled ''APPA 1000 – Total Cost of Ownership for Facilities Asset Management'' incorporates BIM to factor in a variety of critical requirements and costs over the [[Life-cycle assessment|life-cycle]] of the building, including but not limited to: replacement of energy, utility, and safety systems; continual maintenance of the building exterior and interior and replacement of materials; updates to design and functionality; and recapitalization costs.<ref name="Thiemer">{{cite journal |last1=Thiemer |first1=Ana |title=APPA Total Cost of Ownership: The Link to Excellence through Data |journal=Facilities Manager |date=January–February 2022 |url=https://www.appa.org/facilities-manager/appa-total-cost-of-ownership-the-link-to-excellence-through-data/ |access-date=8 January 2024}}</ref>

=== BIM in green building ===
{{main|Building information modeling in green building}}
BIM in [[green building]], or "green BIM", is a process that can help architecture, engineering and construction firms to improve sustainability in the built environment. It can allow architects and engineers to integrate and analyze environmental issues in their design over the [[Life-cycle assessment|life cycle]] of the asset.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1 January 2017|title=Sustainability Assessment through Green BIM for Environmental, Social and Economic Efficiency|journal=Procedia Engineering|language=en|volume=180|pages=520–530|doi=10.1016/j.proeng.2017.04.211|issn=1877-7058|last1=Maltese|first1=Sebastiano|last2=Tagliabue|first2=Lavinia C.|last3=Cecconi|first3=Fulvio Re|last4=Pasini|first4=Daniela|last5=Manfren|first5=Massimiliano|last6=Ciribini|first6=Angelo L.C.|doi-access=free|hdl=11311/1027035|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
In the ERANet projects EPC4SES<ref>https://eranet-smartenergysystems.eu/global/images/cms/Content/Fact%20Sheets/ERANetSES_ProjectFactSheet_RegSys2018_EPC4SES.pdf Project Sheet</ref> and FinSESCo projects worked on the digital representation of the energy demand of the building. The nucleus is the [[XML]] from issuing [[Energy Performance Certificate]]s, amended by roof data to be able to retrieve the position and size of [[Photovoltaics|PV]] or [[PV/T]].

==International developments==
{{Update|section|date=January 2022}}

===Asia===

==== China ====
China began its exploration on informatisation in 2001. The Ministry of Construction announced BIM was the key application technology of informatisation in ''"Ten new technologies of construction industry"'' (by 2010).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Bingsheng |last2=Wang |first2=Min |last3=Zhang |first3=Yutao |last4=Liu |first4=Rui |last5=Wang |first5=Anmin |date=2017 |title=Review and Prospect of BIM Policy in China |journal=IOP Conference Series: Materials Science and Engineering |volume=245 |issue=2 |article-number=022021 |publisher=[[IOP Publishing]] |doi=10.1088/1757-899X/245/2/022021 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2017MS&E..245b2021L }}</ref> The Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST) clearly announced BIM technology as a national key research and application project in ''"12th Five-Year" Science and Technology Development Planning.'' Therefore, the year 2011 was described as ''"The First Year of China's BIM"''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.most.gov.cn/eng/|title=Ministry of Science and Technology of the People's Republic of China|website=most.gov.cn|access-date=9 December 2018|archive-date=6 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206161723/http://www.most.gov.cn/eng/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Hong Kong====
In 2006 the [[Hong Kong Housing Authority]] introduced BIM,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Building Information Modelling {{!}} Hong Kong Housing Authority and Housing Department|url=https://www.housingauthority.gov.hk/en/business-partnerships/resources/building-information-modelling/|access-date=25 January 2022|website=Hong Kong Housing Authority}}</ref> and then set a target of full BIM implementation in 2014/2015. BuildingSmart Hong Kong was inaugurated in Hong Kong SAR in late April 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://buildingsmart.org.hk/blank-1 |title=About bSHK |access-date=28 January 2019 |archive-date=29 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129010750/https://www.buildingsmart.org.hk/blank-1 |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Government of Hong Kong]] mandates the use of BIM for all government projects over HK$30M since 1 January 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.devb.gov.hk/filemanager/technicalcirculars/en/upload/354/1/C-2017-07-01.pdf|title=Adoption of Building Information Modelling for Capital Works Projects in Hong Kong|last=Government of the Hong Kong SAR|date=2017|website=Development Bureau|access-date=8 November 2018|ref=DEVB(W) 430/80/01|archive-date=8 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108105315/https://www.devb.gov.hk/filemanager/technicalcirculars/en/upload/354/1/C-2017-07-01.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

====India====
India Building Information Modelling Association (IBIMA) is a national-level society that represents the entire Indian BIM community.<ref>{{Cite web |title=India BIM Association |url=https://www.ibima.co.in/ |access-date=20 October 2022 |website=IBIMA |language=en}}</ref> In India BIM is also known as VDC: '''V'''irtual '''D'''esign and '''C'''onstruction. Due to its population and economic growth, India has an expanding construction market. In spite of this, BIM usage was reported by only 22% of respondents in a 2014 survey.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fig.net/pub/fig2014/ppt/ss36/ss36_kavanagh_7434.pdf|title=Sawhney, Anil et al. (2014). State of BIM Adoption and Outlook in India (English). RICS School of the Built Environment, Amity University. Noida, Uttar Pradesh.|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=15 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215061819/http://www.fig.net/pub/fig2014/ppt/ss36/ss36_kavanagh_7434.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2019, government officials said BIM could help save up to 20% by shortening construction time, and urged wider adoption by infrastructure ministries.<ref name="Haidar">{{cite news |last1=Haidar |first1=Faizan |title=Government backs new tech to speed up infra work |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/infrastructure/government-backs-new-tech-to-speed-up-infra-work/articleshow/72989656.cms |access-date=15 October 2020 |work=The Economic Times |date=27 December 2019 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017230719/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/infrastructure/government-backs-new-tech-to-speed-up-infra-work/articleshow/72989656.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Iran====
The Iran Building Information Modeling Association (IBIMA) was founded in 2012 by professional engineers from five universities in Iran, including the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department at [[Amirkabir University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ibima.ir/ |title=IRAN Building Information Modeling Association (IBIMA), Tehran, IRAN. |publisher=Ibima.ir |access-date=17 October 2014 |archive-date=21 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021215928/http://www.ibima.ir/}}</ref> While it is not currently active, IBIMA aims to share knowledge resources to support construction engineering management decision-making.<ref name="Hosseini, et al">{{cite web|last1=Hosseini|first1=Reza|last2=Azari|first2=Ehsan|last3=Tivendale|first3=Linda|last4=Chileshe|first4=Nicholas|title=Building Information Modeling (BIM) in Iran: An Exploratory Study (April 2016)|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/304822542|website=Researchgate|access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="Hossein, et al (2)">{{cite web|last1=Hosseini|first1=Reza|last2=Azari|first2=Ehsan|last3=Tivendale|first3=Linda|last4=Chileshe|first4=Nicholas|title=Barriers to adoption of building information modeling (BIM) in Iran: Preliminary results (September 2016)|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281209928|website=Researchgate|access-date=4 December 2016}}</ref>

====Malaysia====
BIM implementation is targeted towards BIM Stage 2 by the year 2020 led by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB Malaysia). Under the Construction Industry Transformation Plan (CITP 2016–2020),<ref>{{Cite web|title = CITP|url=http://www.citp.my/|website = citp.my|access-date = 12 February 2016|last = CITP|archive-date = 11 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311160125/http://www.citp.my/|url-status = live}}</ref> it is hoped more emphasis on technology adoption across the project life-cycle will induce higher productivity.

====Singapore====
The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) has announced that BIM would be introduced for architectural submission (by 2013), structural and M&E submissions (by 2014) and eventually for plan submissions of all projects with gross floor area of more than 5,000 square meters by 2015. The BCA Academy is training students in BIM.<ref>''[http://www.bca.gov.sg/publications/BuildSmart/others/buildsmart_11issue9.pdf BuildSmart] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102051344/http://www.bca.gov.sg/publications/BuildSmart/others/buildsmart_11issue9.pdf |date=2 November 2013 }}'' (BCA magazine), December 2011.</ref>

==== Japan ====
The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MLIT) has announced "Start of BIM pilot project in government building and repairs" (by 2010).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mlit.go.jp/en/index.html|title=Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism|website=mlit.go.jp|access-date=9 December 2018|archive-date=10 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210063250/http://www.mlit.go.jp/en/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Japan Institute of Architects (JIA) released the BIM guidelines (by 2012), which showed the agenda and expected effect of BIM to architects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jia.or.jp/english/|title=English Site｜The Japan Institute of Architects|website=jia.or.jp|access-date=9 December 2018|archive-date=14 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214030123/http://www.jia.or.jp/english/|url-status=live}}</ref> MLIT announced " BIM will be mandated for all of its public works from the fiscal year of 2023, except those having particular reasons". The works subject to WTO Government Procurement Agreement shall comply with the published ISO standards related to BIM such as ISO19650 series as determined by the Article 10 (Technical Specification) of the Agreement.

====South Korea====
Small BIM-related seminars and independent BIM effort existed in South Korea even in the 1990s. However, it was not until the late 2000s that the Korean industry paid attention to BIM. The first industry-level BIM conference was held in April 2008, after which, BIM has been spread very rapidly. Since 2010, the Korean government has been gradually increasing the scope of BIM-mandated projects. McGraw Hill published a detailed report in 2012 on the status of BIM adoption and implementation in South Korea.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://analyticsstore.construction.com/index.php/2012-business-value-of-bim-in-korea-smartmarket-report-english.html|title=Lee, G., J. Lee, et al. (2012). 2012 Business Value of BIM in South Korea (English). SmartMarket Report. Bedford, MA, McGraw Hill Construction.|publisher=Analyticstore.construction.com|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=15 February 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130215183028/http://analyticsstore.construction.com/index.php/2012-business-value-of-bim-in-korea-smartmarket-report-english.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====United Arab Emirates====
[[Dubai Municipality]] issued a circular (196) in 2014 mandating BIM use for buildings of a certain size, height or type. The one page circular initiated strong interest in BIM and the market responded in preparation for more guidelines and direction. In 2015 the Municipality issued another circular (207) titled 'Regarding the expansion of applying the (BIM) on buildings and facilities in the emirate of Dubai' which made BIM mandatory on more projects by reducing the minimum size and height requirement for projects requiring BIM. This second circular drove BIM adoption further with several projects and organizations adopting UK BIM standards as best practice. In 2016, the UAE's Quality and [[Conformity]] Commission set up a BIM steering group to investigate statewide adoption of BIM.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.constructionweekonline.com/article-36590-bim-summit-2015-calls-for-greater-co-operation/|title=BIM Summit 2015 calls for greater co-operation|newspaper=Construction Week Online |date=6 December 2015 |publisher=ConstructionWeekOnline.com|access-date=6 December 2015|archive-date=13 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151213062150/http://www.constructionweekonline.com/article-36590-bim-summit-2015-calls-for-greater-co-operation/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Europe===

====Austria====
Austrian standards for digital modeling are summarized in the ÖNORM A 6241, published on 15 March 2015. The ÖNORM A 6241-1 (BIM Level 2), which replaced the ÖNORM A 6240-4, has been extended in the detailed and executive design stages, and corrected in the lack of definitions. The ÖNORM A 6241-2 (BIM Level 3) includes all the requirements for the BIM Level 3 (iBIM).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.austrian-standards.at/infopedia-themencenter/infopedia-artikel/building-information-modeling-bim/|title=Building information modelling (BIM)|publisher=austrian-standards.at|access-date=22 March 2016|archive-date=11 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311203255/https://www.austrian-standards.at/infopedia-themencenter/infopedia-artikel/building-information-modeling-bim/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Czech Republic====
The Czech BIM Council, established in May 2011, aims to implement BIM methodologies into the Czech building and designing processes, education, standards and legislation.<ref name="BIMhubcz">{{cite web|title=Czech BIM Council|url=https://thebimhub.com/companies/czech-bim-council-5/#.WFeY3xuLRnI|website=The BIM Hub|access-date=19 December 2016|archive-date=22 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222105354/https://thebimhub.com/companies/czech-bim-council-5/#.WFeY3xuLRnI|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

====Estonia====
In Estonia digital construction cluster (Digitaalehituse Klaster) was formed in 2015 to develop BIM solutions for the whole life-cycle of construction.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://e-difice.com/en/|title=cluster of digital construction|publisher=digitaalehitus.ee|access-date=5 June 2016|archive-date=5 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605223539/http://e-difice.com/en/|url-status=live}}</ref> The strategic objective of the cluster is to develop an innovative digital construction environment as well as VDC [[new product development]], Grid and e-construction portal to increase the international competitiveness and sales of Estonian businesses in the construction field. The cluster is equally co-funded by European Structural and Investment Funds through Enterprise Estonia and by the members of the cluster with a total budget of 600 000 euros for the period 2016–2018.

====France====
The French arm of [[buildingSMART]], called Mediaconstruct (existing since 1989), is supporting digital transformation in France. A building transition digital plan – French acronym PTNB – was created in 2013 (mandated since 2015 to 2017 and under several ministries). A 2013 survey of European BIM practice showed France in last place, but, with government support, in 2017 it had risen to third place with more than 30% of real estate projects carried out using BIM.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.blog-logiciel-btp.com/le-bim-en-france-ou-en-est-on/ | title=BIM and France | date=26 November 2018 | access-date=22 November 2021 | archive-date=22 November 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122210840/https://www.blog-logiciel-btp.com/le-bim-en-france-ou-en-est-on | url-status=live }}</ref> PTNB was superseded in 2018 by Plan BIM 2022,<ref name="Nicolas=20Nov2018">{{cite news |last1=Nicolas |first1=Julie |title=Le PTNB est mort, vive le Plan BIM 2022 |url=https://www.lemoniteur.fr/article/le-ptnb-est-mort-vive-le-plan-bim-2022.2005309 |access-date=22 November 2021 |work=Le Moniteur |date=20 November 2018 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122145704/https://www.lemoniteur.fr/article/le-ptnb-est-mort-vive-le-plan-bim-2022.2005309 |url-status=live }}</ref> administered by an industry body, the Association for the Development of Digital in Construction (AND Construction), founded in 2017, and supported by a digital platform, KROQI,<ref name="GlobalBIM-Kroqi">{{cite web |title=KROQi Web Platform |url=https://www.globalbim.org/information-collection/kroqi-web-platform |website=Global BIM |access-date=22 November 2021 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122151918/https://www.globalbim.org/information-collection/kroqi-web-platform |url-status=live }}</ref> developed and launched in 2017 by CSTB (France's [[Scientific and Technical Centre for Building]]).<ref name="CSTB">{{cite web |title=Multi-scale BIM for all |url=http://www.cstb.fr/rapport-activite/2017/en/challenges/3/intro |website=CSTB |access-date=22 November 2021 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122154017/http://www.cstb.fr/rapport-activite/2017/en/challenges/3/intro/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Germany====
In December 2015, the German minister for transport [[Alexander Dobrindt]] announced a timetable for the introduction of mandatory BIM for German road and rail projects from the end of 2020.<ref name=Crunch>{{cite news|last1=White|first1=Jack|title=BIM mandate for transport projects in Germany confirmed for 2020|url=http://bimcrunch.com/2015/12/bim-mandate-for-transport-projects-in-germany-confirmed-for-2020/|access-date=17 December 2015|work=BIM Crunch|date=16 December 2015|archive-date=14 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114184256/http://bimcrunch.com/2015/12/bim-mandate-for-transport-projects-in-germany-confirmed-for-2020/|url-status=live}}</ref> Speaking in April 2016, he said digital design and construction must become standard for construction projects in Germany, with Germany two to three years behind The Netherlands and the UK in aspects of implementing BIM.<ref name="BIMHub">{{cite web|title=BIM must become standard for construction in Germany says minister|url=https://thebimhub.com/2016/04/12/bim-must-become-standard-construction-germany-says|website=The BIM Hub|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=4 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604115550/https://thebimhub.com/2016/04/12/bim-must-become-standard-construction-germany-says/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> BIM was piloted in many areas of German infrastructure delivery and in July 2022 [[Volker Wissing]], [[Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport|Federal Minister for Digital and Transport]], announced that, from 2025, BIM will be used as standard in the construction of federal trunk roads in addition to the rail sector.<ref name="BMDV-06Jul2022">{{cite news |title=Federal cabinet decides on digitization measures to speed up planning and approval |url=https://bmdv.bund.de/SharedDocs/DE/Pressemitteilungen/2022/046-bundeskabinett-beschliesst-digitalisierungsmassnahmen.html |access-date=8 August 2022 |work=Ministry for Digital Affairs and Transport |date=6 July 2022}}</ref>

====Ireland====
In November 2017, Ireland's Department for Public Expenditure and Reform launched a strategy to increase use of digital technology in delivery of key public works projects, requiring the use of BIM to be phased in over the next four years.<ref name="PER">{{cite news |title=Government Strategy to Increase use of Digital Technology in Key Public Works Projects Launched |url=https://www.per.gov.ie/en/government-strategy-to-increase-use-of-digital-technology-in-key-public-works-projects-launched/ |access-date=30 July 2018 |work=National Development Plan, 2018 – 2027 |publisher=Department of Public Expenditure and Reform |date=21 November 2017 |archive-date=30 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730112557/https://www.per.gov.ie/en/government-strategy-to-increase-use-of-digital-technology-in-key-public-works-projects-launched/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Italy====
Through the new D.l. 50, in April 2016 Italy has included into its own legislation several European directives including 2014/24/EU on Public Procurement. The decree states among the main goals of public procurement the "rationalization of designing activities and of all connected verification processes, through the progressive adoption of digital methods and electronic instruments such as Building and Infrastructure Information Modelling".<ref>D.lgs. 50/2016, art. 23 com. 1 lett. h</ref><ref>[https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaDettaglioAtto/originario?atto.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2016-04-19&atto.codiceRedazionale=16G00062 DECRETO LEGISLATIVO 18 aprile 2016, n. 50] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125212639/https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaDettaglioAtto/originario?atto.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2016-04-19&atto.codiceRedazionale=16G00062 |date=25 January 2021 }} Gazzetta Ufficiale. Retrieved: 3 December 2021.</ref> A norm in 8 parts is also being written to support the transition: UNI 11337-1, UNI 11337-4 and UNI 11337-5 were published in January 2017, with five further chapters to follow within a year.

In early 2018 the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport issued a decree (DM 01/12/17) creating a governmental BIM Mandate compelling public client organisations to adopt a digital approach by 2025, with an incremental obligation which will start on 1 January 2019.<ref name="Ciribini-21Mar2018">{{cite news|last1=Ciribini|first1=Angelo|last2=De Giuda|first2=Giuseppe|last3=Valaguzza|first3=Sara|title=UK PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK INFORMS ITALY'S MOVE TO MANDATE BIM|url=http://www.bimplus.co.uk/people/uk-procurement-framework-informs-italys-move-manda/|access-date=22 March 2018|work=BIM Plus|date=21 March 2018|archive-date=21 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321122045/http://www.bimplus.co.uk/people/uk-procurement-framework-informs-italys-move-manda/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mit.gov.it/normativa/decreto-ministeriale-numero-560-del-01122017|title=Decreto Ministeriale numero 560 del 01/12/2017 {{!}} mit|website=mit.gov.it|access-date=20 January 2019|archive-date=19 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119174310/http://www.mit.gov.it/normativa/decreto-ministeriale-numero-560-del-01122017|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Lithuania====
Lithuania is moving towards adoption of BIM infrastructure by founding a public body "Skaitmeninė statyba" (Digital Construction), which is managed by 13 associations. Also, there is a BIM work group established by Lietuvos Architektų Sąjunga (a Lithuanian architects body). The initiative intends Lithuania to adopt BIM, Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) and National Construction Classification as standard. An international conference "Skaitmeninė statyba Lietuvoje" (Digital Construction in Lithuania) has been held annually since 2012.

====The Netherlands====
On 1 November 2011, the Rijksgebouwendienst, the agency within the [[Ministry of Housing, Spatial Planning and the Environment|Dutch Ministry of Housing, Spatial Planning and the Environment]] that manages government buildings, introduced the Rgd BIM Standard,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rgd.nl/onderwerpen/diensten/bouwwerk-informatie-modellen-bim/rgd-bim-norm/#c16783|title=Vastgoed van en voor het Rijk|publisher=Rgd.nl|access-date=17 October 2014|date=14 May 2013|archive-date=6 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130306103218/http://www.rgd.nl/onderwerpen/diensten/bouwwerk-informatie-modellen-bim/rgd-bim-norm/#c16783|url-status=live}}</ref> which it updated on 1 July 2012.

====Norway====
In Norway BIM has been used increasingly since 2008. Several large public clients require use of BIM in open formats (IFC) in most or all of their projects. The Government Building Authority bases its processes on BIM in open formats to increase process speed and quality, and all large and several small and medium-sized contractors use BIM. National BIM development is centred around the local organisation, buildingSMART Norway which represents 25% of the Norwegian construction industry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patel |first=Akash |title=BIM Adoption in Scandinavia |url=https://www.united-bim.com/blog/bim-adoption-in-scandinavia |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908091219/https://www.united-bim.com/blog/bim-adoption-in-scandinavia |archive-date=8 September 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026 |website=United-BIM |publisher=United-BIM}}</ref>

====Poland====
BIMKlaster (BIM Cluster) is a non-governmental, non-profit organisation established in 2012 with the aim of promoting BIM development in Poland.<ref name="BIMKlaster">{{cite web|title=BIMKlaster|url=http://www.bimklaster.org.pl/?lang=en|website=BIMKlaster.org.pl|access-date=24 February 2017|archive-date=26 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170226172923/http://www.bimklaster.org.pl/?lang=en|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2016, the Ministry of Infrastructure and Construction began a series of expert meetings concerning the application of BIM methodologies in the construction industry.<ref name="KPMG">{{cite web|last1=KPMG and Arup|title=Building Information Modeling: Ekspertyza dotycząca możliwości wdrożenia metodyki BIM w Polsce ("Building Information Modeling. Expertise concerning the possibility of implementing BIM methodology in Poland")|url=http://mib.gov.pl/files/0/1797409/mozliwosciwdrozeniametodykiBIM.pdf|website=MIB.gov.pl|access-date=24 February 2017|archive-date=20 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220175239/http://mib.gov.pl/files/0/1797409/mozliwosciwdrozeniametodykiBIM.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Portugal====
Created in 2015 to promote the adoption of BIM in Portugal and its normalisation, the Technical Committee for BIM Standardisation, CT197-BIM, has created the first strategic document for construction 4.0 in Portugal, aiming to align the country's industry around a common vision, integrated and more ambitious than a simple technology change.<ref name="BIMplus-4Dec2016">{{cite news|last1=Aguiar Costa|first1=Antonio|title=Construction 4.0 in Portugal|url=http://www.bimplus.co.uk/people/con2st6ruction-40-portu5gal/|access-date=6 December 2016|work=Construction Manager: BIM+|date=4 December 2016|archive-date=5 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161205125722/http://www.bimplus.co.uk/people/con2st6ruction-40-portu5gal/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Russia====

The Russian government has approved a list of the regulations that provide the creation of a legal framework for the use of information modeling of buildings in construction and encourages the use of BIM in government projects.<ref>Shubin, Nikolai (2015) [https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/38130432.pdf Possibilities of BIM in Russia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414164234/https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/38130432.pdf |date=14 April 2019 }}. Accessed: 14 April 2021.</ref>

====Slovakia====
The BIM Association of Slovakia, "BIMaS", was established in January 2013 as the first Slovak professional organisation focused on BIM. Although there are neither standards nor legislative requirements to deliver projects in BIM, many architects, structural engineers and contractors, plus a few investors are already applying BIM. A Slovak implementation strategy created by BIMaS and supported by the Chamber of Civil Engineers and Chamber of Architects has yet to be approved by Slovak authorities due to their low interest in such innovation.<ref>[https://www.bimas.sk BIMaS.sk] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110135328/https://www.bimas.sk/ |date=10 November 2021 }}, BIMaS website. Accessed: 4 September 2015.</ref>

====Spain====
A July 2015 meeting at Spain's Ministry of Infrastructure [Ministerio de Fomento] launched the country's national BIM strategy, making BIM a mandatory requirement on public sector projects with a possible starting date of 2018.<ref name=BIMplusSpain>{{cite news|last1=Knutt|first1=Elaine|title=Spain launches BIM strategy with pencilled-in 2018 mandate|url=http://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/spain-launches-bim-strategy-pencilled-2018-mandate/|access-date=20 August 2015|work=Construction Manager: BIMplus|date=16 July 2015|archive-date=3 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150803104926/http://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/spain-launches-bim-strategy-pencilled-2018-mandate/|url-status=live}}</ref> Following a February 2015 BIM summit in Barcelona, professionals in Spain established a BIM commission (ITeC) to drive the adoption of BIM in Catalonia.<ref name="ITeC">{{cite web|title=La Comissió Construïm el Futur (transl: The Commission Building the Future)|url=https://itec.cat/serveis/bim/comissio-construim-el-futur/|website=ITeC|access-date=7 July 2017|archive-date=8 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708121932/https://itec.cat/serveis/bim/comissio-construim-el-futur/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Switzerland====
Since 2009 through the initiative of buildingSmart Switzerland, then 2013, BIM awareness among a broader community of engineers and architects was raised due to the open competition for [[Basel]]'s Felix Platter Hospital<ref>[http://www.felixplatterspital.ch/fileadmin/pdf/Neubau/Gesamtleistungswettbewerb_Felix_Platter_Spital_simap.pdf]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110135358/http://www.felixplatterspital.ch/fileadmin/pdf/Neubau/Gesamtleistungswettbewerb_Felix_Platter_Spital_simap.pdf|date=10 November 2013}}</ref> where a BIM coordinator was sought. BIM has also been a subject of events by the Swiss Society for Engineers and Architects, SIA.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sia.ch/de/der-sia/berufsgruppen/technik/jahrestagung-2013|title=jahrestagung 2013 – sia – schweizerischer ingenieur- und architektenverein|work=sia – schweizerischer ingenieur- und architektenverein|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=10 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110145709/http://www.sia.ch/de/der-sia/berufsgruppen/technik/jahrestagung-2013/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====United Kingdom====
In May 2011 UK Government [[Chief Construction Adviser to UK Government|Chief Construction Adviser]] [[Paul Morrell]] called for BIM adoption on UK government construction projects.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thenbs.com/roundtable/|title=BIM Roundtable Discussion|publisher=Thenbs.com|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=22 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022210225/http://www.thenbs.com/roundtable/|url-status=live}}</ref> Morrell also told construction professionals to adopt BIM or be "Betamaxed out".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bdonline.co.uk/news/adopt-bim-or-be-betamaxed-out-says-morrell/5018263.article|title=Adopt bim or be 'Betamaxed out' says Morrell|work=Building Design|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=22 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022164545/http://www.bdonline.co.uk/news/adopt-bim-or-be-betamaxed-out-says-morrell/5018263.article|url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2011 the UK government published its BIM strategy,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ktn.innovateuk.org/web/modernbuiltktn/articles/-/blogs/new-construction-strategy?ns_33_redirect=%2Fweb%2Fmodernbuiltktn%2Farticles|title=Modern Built Environment – innovateuk|publisher=Ktn.innovateuk.org|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> announcing its intention to require collaborative 3D BIM (with all project and asset information, documentation and data being electronic) on its projects by 2016. Initially, compliance would require building data to be delivered in a vendor-neutral '[[COBie]]' format, thus overcoming the limited interoperability of BIM software suites available on the market. The UK Government [[BIM Task Group]] led the government's BIM programme and requirements,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bimtaskgroup.org/|title=BIM Task Group – A UK Government Initiative|publisher=Bimtaskgroup.org|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=17 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017171041/http://www.bimtaskgroup.org/|url-status=live}}</ref> including a free-to-use set of UK standards and tools that defined 'level 2 BIM'.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://toolkit.thenbs.com/articles/the-level-2-bim-package|title=The level-2 BIM package|publisher=BIM Task Group|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-date=18 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518080243/https://toolkit.thenbs.com/articles/the-level-2-bim-package|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2016, the UK Government published a new central web portal as a point of reference for the industry for 'level 2 BIM'.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bim-level2.org/|title=BIM Level 2|publisher=BSI Group|access-date=19 April 2016|archive-date=5 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405024607/http://bim-level2.org/|url-status=live}}</ref> The work of the BIM Task Group then continued under the stewardship of the [[Cambridge]]-based [[Centre for Digital Built Britain]] (CDBB),<ref name="BIM L2 FAQs">{{cite web |title=What Was the UK BIM Task Group? |url=https://bim-level2.org/en/faqs/ |website=BIM Level 2 |access-date=19 July 2019 |archive-date=19 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190719100957/https://bim-level2.org/en/faqs/ |url-status=live }}</ref> announced in December 2017 and formally launched in early 2018.<ref name="Williamson-01Dec2017">{{cite news |last1=Williamson |first1=Jonny |title=£5.4m to launch 'Centre for Digital Built Britain' |access-date=19 July 2019 |work=The Manufacturer |url=https://www.themanufacturer.com/articles/5-4m-to-launch-centre-for-digital-built-britain/ |date=1 December 2017 |archive-date=19 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190719102940/https://www.themanufacturer.com/articles/5-4m-to-launch-centre-for-digital-built-britain/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Outside of government, industry adoption of BIM since 2016 has been led by the UK BIM Alliance,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ukbimalliance.org/|title=UK BIM Alliance|website=ukbimalliance.org|access-date=17 November 2017|archive-date=19 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171119074717/http://www.ukbimalliance.org/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> an independent, not-for-profit, collaboratively-based organisation formed to champion and enable the implementation of BIM, and to connect and represent organisations, groups and individuals working towards digital transformation of the UK's built environment industry. In November 2017, the UK BIM Alliance merged with the UK and Ireland chapter of BuildingSMART.<ref name="BIMp-5Nov2017">{{cite news |title=UK BIM Alliance and buildingSMART to merge |url=http://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/uk-bim-alliance-and-buildingsmart-merge/ |access-date=21 January 2019 |work=BIM plus |publisher=CIOB |date=5 November 2017 |archive-date=21 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121175215/http://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/uk-bim-alliance-and-buildingsmart-merge/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In October 2019, CDBB, the UK BIM Alliance (since October 2022, known as 'nima'<ref name="Stanton-03Oct2022">{{cite news |last1=Stanton |first1=Justin |title=Nima: UK BIM Alliance puts information management first with new name, new approach |url=https://www.bimplus.co.uk/nima-uk-bim-alliance-puts-information-management-first-with-new-name-new-approach/ |access-date=18 October 2022 |work=BIM plus |date=3 October 2022}}</ref>) and the [[BSI Group]] launched the UK BIM Framework. Superseding the BIM levels approach, the framework describes an overarching approach to implementing BIM in the UK, giving free guidance on integrating the international [[ISO 19650]] series of standards into UK processes and practice.<ref name="PBC-17Oct2019">{{cite news |title=UK BIM Alliance, BSI & CDBB launch UK BIM Framework |url=https://www.pbctoday.co.uk/news/bim-news/uk-bim-framework/65207/ |access-date=19 May 2020 |work=PBC Today |date=17 October 2019 |archive-date=8 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608080405/https://www.pbctoday.co.uk/news/bim-news/uk-bim-framework/65207/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The CDBB closed in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dickson |first=Jo |date=2022-03-28 |title=Celebrating Mission Complete |url=https://www.cdbb.cam.ac.uk/news/celebrating-mission-complete-0 |access-date=2022-05-06 |website=www.cdbb.cam.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

[[National Building Specification]] (NBS) has published research into BIM adoption in the UK since 2011, and in 2020 published its 10th annual BIM report.<ref name="NBS10-01Jun2020">{{cite web |title=NBS' 10th National BIM Report |url=https://www.thenbs.com/bim-report-2020 |website=NBS |access-date=1 June 2020 |archive-date=8 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608013910/https://www.thenbs.com/bim-report-2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2011, 43% of respondents had not heard of BIM; in 2020 73% said they were using BIM.<ref name="NBS10-01Jun2020"/>

===North America===

====Canada====
BIM is not mandatory in Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 October 2019 |title=BIM can transform the Canadian construction and design industry - constructconnect.com |url=https://canada.constructconnect.com/dcn/news/government/2019/10/bim-can-transform-the-canadian-construction-and-design-industry |access-date=2 February 2023 |website=Daily Commercial News |language=en-US}}</ref> Several organizations support BIM adoption and implementation in Canada: the Canada BIM Council (CANBIM, founded in 2008),<ref name="Canada BIM Council">{{cite web |url=http://www.canbim.com/ |title=Canada BIM Council |access-date=1 July 2013 |archive-date=26 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130726233613/http://www.canbim.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> the Institute for BIM in Canada,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ibc-bim.ca/ |title=Institute for BIM in Canada (IBC) |access-date=29 September 2015 |archive-date=1 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001021925/https://www.ibc-bim.ca/ |url-status=usurped }}</ref> and buildingSMART Canada (the Canadian chapter of [[buildingSMART]] International).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.buildingsmartcanada.ca/ |title=buildingSMART Canada |access-date=22 September 2015 |archive-date=1 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001192531/https://www.buildingsmartcanada.ca/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Public Services and Procurement Canada]] (formerly Public Works and Government Services Canada) is committed to using non-proprietary or "OpenBIM" BIM standards and avoids specifying any specific proprietary BIM format. Designers are required to use the international standards of interoperability for BIM (IFC).<ref>Public Services and Procurement Canada, [https://buyandsell.gc.ca/cds/public/2021/04/29/e6a9e9fefe68d47b818ea4bee85fb371/ABES.PROD.PW_PWL.B034.E2562.ATTA001.PDF Doing Business with PWGSC: Documentation and Deliverables Manual], updated 31 January 2019, accessed 28 January 2024</ref>

====United States====
[[File:Architectural BIM 3D Modeling.jpg|thumb|Architectural BIM Modeling of Clinton Public Library, USA]]
The [[Associated General Contractors of America]] and US contracting firms have developed various working definitions of BIM that describe it generally as:

:''an object-oriented building development tool that utilizes 5-D modeling concepts, information technology and software interoperability to design, construct and operate a building project, as well as communicate its details.''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.necanet.org/downloads/pdf/about/meet/academy/academy-2010-presentation.pdf|title=The Future Is Now! Building Information Modeling (BIM)|website=necanet.org|access-date=14 April 2021|archive-date=14 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414103108/http://apps.necanet.org/downloads/pdf/about/meet/academy/academy-2010-presentation.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

Although the concept of BIM and relevant processes are being explored by contractors, architects and [[real estate developers|developers]] alike, the term itself has been questioned and debated<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aecbytes.com/newsletter/2004/issue_5.html|title=AECbytes Archived Articles|publisher=Aecbytes.com|access-date=17 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021134606/http://www.aecbytes.com/newsletter/2004/issue_5.html|archive-date=21 October 2014}}</ref> with alternatives including Virtual Building Environment (VBE) also considered. Unlike some countries such as the UK, the US has not adopted a set of national BIM guidelines, allowing different systems to remain in competition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.architectmagazine.com/technology/setting-a-standard-in-building-information-modeling_o|title=Setting a Standard in Building Information Modeling (Architect Magazine)|last=Shapiro|first=Gideon Fink|date=2 May 2014|website=architectmagazine.com|access-date=21 March 2018|archive-date=22 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322020923/http://www.architectmagazine.com/technology/setting-a-standard-in-building-information-modeling_o|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2021, the [[National Institute of Building Sciences]] (NIBS) looked at applying UK BIM experiences to developing shared US BIM standards and processes. The US National BIM Standard had largely been developed through volunteer efforts; NIBS aimed to create a national BIM programme to drive effective adoption at a national scale.<ref name="BIM+-16Feb2021">{{cite news |title=UK helps US with BIM adoption |url=https://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/uk-helps-us-bim-adoption/ |access-date=18 February 2021 |work=BIM Plus |date=16 February 2021 |archive-date=17 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217195324/https://www.bimplus.co.uk/news/uk-helps-us-bim-adoption/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

BIM is seen to be closely related to [[Integrated project delivery|Integrated Project Delivery]] (IPD) where the primary motive is to bring the teams together early on in the project.<ref>AIA, C.C., A working Definition: Integrated Project Delivery. 2007, McGraw Hill Construction{{page needed|date=January 2012}}</ref> A full implementation of BIM also requires the project teams to collaborate from the inception stage and formulate model sharing and ownership contract documents.

The [[American Institute of Architects]] has defined BIM as "a model-based technology linked with a database of project information",{{ref|definition}} and this reflects the general reliance on database technology as the foundation. In the future, structured text documents such as [[specifications]] may be able to be searched and linked to regional, national, and international standards.

===Africa===

====Nigeria====
BIM has the potential to play a vital role in the Nigerian AEC sector. In addition to its potential clarity and transparency, it may help promote standardization across the industry. For instance, Utiome<ref>Utiome, Erezi, Drogemuller, Robin, & Docherty, Michael (2014). [http://eprints.qut.edu.au/76076/ "BIM-based lifecycle planning and specifications for sustainable cities of the future : a conceptual approach"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150113062815/http://eprints.qut.edu.au/76076/ |date=13 January 2015 }}</ref> suggests that, in conceptualizing a BIM-based knowledge transfer framework from industrialized economies to urban construction projects in developing nations, generic BIM objects can benefit from rich building information within specification parameters in product libraries, and used for efficient, streamlined design and construction. Similarly, an assessment of the current 'state of the art' by Kori<ref>Kori, S. (2013). Toward Adoption of Building Information Modelling in the Nigeria AEC industry. MSc, University of Salford, Manchester.</ref> found that medium and large firms were leading the adoption of BIM in the industry. Smaller firms were less advanced with respect to process and policy adherence. There has been little adoption of BIM in the built environment due to construction industry resistance to changes or new ways of doing things. The industry is still working with conventional 2D CAD systems in services and structural designs, although production could be in 3D systems. There is virtually no utilisation of 4D and 5D systems.

BIM Africa Initiative, primarily based in Nigeria, is a non-profit institute advocating the adoption of BIM across Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bimafrica.org/ | title=BIM Africa &#124; Advocating the adoption of BIM across Africa | access-date=5 December 2019 | archive-date=5 December 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205135332/https://bimafrica.org/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Since 2018, it has been engaging with professionals and the government towards the digital transformation of the built industry.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.africa.com/driving-digital-transformation-in-west-african-construction-sector/ |title=Driving digital transformation in West African construction sector |access-date=5 December 2019 |archive-date=5 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205135336/https://www.africa.com/driving-digital-transformation-in-west-african-construction-sector/ }}</ref><ref>"[https://www.sunnewsonline.com/bim-to-enhance-building-capacity-create-business-opportunities-nationwide-fashola/ BIM to enhance building capacity, create business opportunities nationwide – Fashola] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205135334/https://www.sunnewsonline.com/bim-to-enhance-building-capacity-create-business-opportunities-nationwide-fashola/ |date=2019-12-05 }}" (28 November 2019) ''The Sun'', Nigeria. Accessed: 11 September 2020.</ref> Produced annually by its research and development committee, the African BIM Report gives an overview of BIM adoption across the African continent.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bimafrica.org/african-bim-report/ | title=The African BIM Report | work=BIM Africa | access-date=5 December 2019 | archive-date=5 December 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205135335/https://bimafrica.org/african-bim-report/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

====South Africa====
The South African BIM Institute, established in May 2015, aims to enable technical experts to discuss digital construction solutions that can be adopted by professionals working within the construction sector. Its initial task was to promote the SA BIM Protocol.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.biminstitute.org.za/ | title=BIM Institute &#124; Africa's voice for Building Information Modelling (BIM) | access-date=19 August 2016 | archive-date=16 August 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816030933/http://www.biminstitute.org.za/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

There are no mandated or national best practice BIM standards or protocols in South Africa. Organisations implement company-specific BIM standards and protocols at best (there are isolated examples of cross-industry alliances).{{citation needed|date=September 2017}}

===Oceania===

====Australia====
In February 2016, Infrastructure Australia recommended: "Governments should make the use of Building Information Modelling (BIM) mandatory for the design of large-scale complex infrastructure projects. In support of a mandatory rollout, the Australian Government should commission the Australasian Procurement and Construction Council, working with industry, to develop appropriate guidance around the adoption and use of BIM; and common standards and protocols to be applied when using BIM".<ref name="BIMCrunchFeb2016">{{cite news|title=Infrastructure Australia recommend BIM mandate for large-scale projects|url=http://bimcrunch.com/2016/02/infrastructure-australia-recommend-bim-mandate-for-large-scale-projects/|access-date=16 August 2016|work=BIM Crunch|date=17 February 2016|archive-date=27 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827002803/http://bimcrunch.com/2016/02/infrastructure-australia-recommend-bim-mandate-for-large-scale-projects/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====New Zealand====
In 2015, many projects in the rebuilding of [[Christchurch]] were being assembled in detail on a computer using BIM well before workers set foot on the site. The New Zealand government started a BIM acceleration committee, as part of a productivity partnership with the goal of 20 per cent more efficiency in the construction industry by 2020.<ref>''New Zealand Herald'', Tuesday 14 April 2015</ref> Today, BIM use is still not mandated in the country while several challenges have been identified for its implementation in the country.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ma |first1=Lijun |last2=Lovreglio |first2=Ruggiero |last3=Yi |first3=Wen |last4=Yiu |first4=Tak Wing |last5=Shan |first5=Ming |date=18 February 2022 |title=Barriers and strategies for building information modelling implementation: a comparative study between New Zealand and China |journal=International Journal of Construction Management |volume=23 |issue=12 |pages=2067–2076 |doi=10.1080/15623599.2022.2040076 |issn=1562-3599|hdl=10179/17494 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> However, members of the AEC industry and academia have developed a national BIM handbook providing definitions, case studies and templates.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BIMinNZ |url=https://www.biminnz.co.nz/ |access-date=13 March 2024 |website=BIMinNZ |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Purposes or dimensionality==
Some purposes or uses of BIM may be described as 'dimensions'. However, there is little consensus on definitions beyond 5D. Some organisations dismiss the term; for example, the UK [[Institution of Structural Engineers]] does not recommend using nD modelling terms beyond 4D, adding "cost (5D) is not really a 'dimension'."<ref name="IStructE">{{cite web |title=BIM guidance part 1: Introduction to BIM |url=https://www.istructe.org/resources/guidance/bim-guidance-part-1-introduction-to-bim/ |website=Institution of Structural Engineers |date=24 April 2020 |publisher=IStructE |access-date=27 May 2020 |archive-date=3 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803210207/https://www.istructe.org/resources/guidance/bim-guidance-part-1-introduction-to-bim/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="IStructE2">{{cite web |title=An Introduction to Building Information Modelling |url=https://www.istructe.org/resources/guidance/an-introduction-to-building-information-modelling// |website=Institution of Structural Engineers |date=23 February 2021 |publisher=IStructE |access-date=5 May 2021 |archive-date=5 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505131947/https://www.istructe.org/resources/guidance/an-introduction-to-building-information-modelling// |url-status=live }}</ref>

===3D===
'''[[3D modeling|3D]] BIM''', an acronym for [[Three-dimensional space|three-dimensional]] building information modeling, refers to the graphical representation of an asset's geometric design, augmented by information describing attributes of individual components. 3D BIM work may be undertaken by professional disciplines such as architectural, structural, and [[Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing|MEP]],<ref name=3DBIM-R-01>{{Cite web|url=https://www.autodesk.com/industry/aec/bim|title=What is BIM|access-date=27 November 2021|archive-date=24 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324171303/https://www.autodesk.com/industry/aec/bim|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=3DBIM-R-02>{{Cite web|url=https://marsbiminternational.com/insights/resources/bim-dimensions/|title=BIM Dimensions|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=2 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220602070852/https://marsbiminternational.com/insights/resources/bim-dimensions/|url-status=live}}</ref> and the use of 3D models enhances coordination and collaboration between disciplines. A 3D virtual model can also be created by creating a [[point cloud]] of the building or facility using [[laser scanning]] technology.<ref name="3DBIM-R-08">{{Cite web|url=https://constructible.trimble.com/detailer/the-basics-of-mep-3d-scanning-point-clouds-and-bim-models-2|title=The Basics of MEP 3D Scanning: Point Clouds and BIM Models|access-date=8 May 2016|archive-date=18 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190818221747/https://constructible.trimble.com/detailer/the-basics-of-mep-3d-scanning-point-clouds-and-bim-models-2|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="3DBIM-R-09">{{cite web|url=https://www.gsa.gov/cdnstatic/GSA_BIM_Guide_Series_03.pdf|title=BIM Guide For 3D Imaging|website=gsa.gov|publisher=General Services Administration|date=12 January 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419101423/https://www.gsa.gov/cdnstatic/GSA_BIM_Guide_Series_03.pdf|archive-date=19 April 2021}}</ref>

===4D===
[[File:4d-bim-simulation-of-waste-water-treatment-plant-project.gif|thumb|4D BIM Construction Simulation]]
'''4D BIM''', an acronym for 4-dimensional building information modeling, refers to the intelligent linking of individual [[3D CAD]] components or assemblies with time- or scheduling-related information.<ref name=4DBIM-R-01>{{Cite web|url=http://structuremag.org/article.aspx?articleID=1234|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120530011123/http://structuremag.org/article.aspx?articleID=1234|archive-date=30 May 2012|title= 4D BIM or Simulation-Based Modeling |publisher=structuremag.org |access-date=9 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Mills|first1=Fred|title=What is 4D BIM?|url=http://www.theb1m.com/video/what-is-4d-bim|website=TheB1M.com|publisher=The B1M Limited|access-date=2 February 2016|archive-date=7 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190307182252/https://www.theb1m.com/video/what-is-4d-bim|url-status=live}}</ref> The term 4D refers to the [[Four-dimensional space|fourth dimension]]: [[Time in physics|time]], i.e. 3D plus time.<ref name="5DBIM-R-02">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cadsoft-consult.com/blogs/architecture/2009/09/ashrae-introduction-to-bim-4d-and-5d/|title=ASHRAE Introduction to BIM, 4D and 5D|publisher=cadsoft-consult.com|access-date=29 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403091827/http://www.cadsoft-consult.com/blogs/architecture/2009/09/ashrae-introduction-to-bim-4d-and-5d/|archive-date=3 April 2013}}</ref>

4D modelling enables project participants (architects, designers, contractors, clients) to plan, sequence the physical activities, visualise the critical path of a series of events, mitigate the risks, report and monitor progress of activities through the lifetime of the project.<ref name="5DBIM-R-03">{{Cite web|url=http://www.wbdg.org/bim/nibs_bim.php|title=NIBS BIM Initiatives|publisher=wbdg.org|access-date=29 May 2012|archive-date=13 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513090937/http://www.wbdg.org/bim/nibs_bim.php}}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-04>{{Cite web |url=http://www.stanford.edu/group/4D/workspace/papers/asce-96.pdf |publisher=stanford.edu |title=Interactive 4D-CAD by Kathleen McKinney, Jennifer Kim, Martin Fischer, Craig Howard |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-date=21 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100821180917/http://www.stanford.edu/group/4D/workspace/papers/asce-96.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="5DBIM-R-04">{{Cite web |url=http://www.stanford.edu/group/4D/ |title=Introduction to 4D Research by Martin Fischer |publisher=stanford.edu |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-date=26 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161126100907/http://stanford.edu/group/4D// |url-status=live }}</ref> 4D BIM enables a sequence of events to be depicted visually on a time line that has been populated by a 3D model, augmenting traditional [[Gantt chart]]s and [[Critical path method|critical path (CPM)]] schedules often used in project management.<ref name=4DBIM-R-16>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gsa.gov/Portal/gsa/ep/channelView.do?pageTypeId=17109&channelPage=/ep/channel/gsaOverview.jsp&channelId=-24291 |title=GSA Web Site |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091112145341/http://www.gsa.gov/Portal/gsa/ep/channelView.do?pageTypeId=17109&channelPage=%2Fep%2Fchannel%2FgsaOverview.jsp&channelId=-24291 |archive-date=12 November 2009 }}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-17>{{Cite web |url=http://www.precisionschedulingconsultants.com/4D_BIM_The_Evolution_of_Construction_Scheduling.html |title=4D BIM: The Evolution of Construction Scheduling |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-date=8 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608110448/http://www.precisionschedulingconsultants.com/4D_BIM_The_Evolution_of_Construction_Scheduling.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-18>{{Cite web |url=http://www.architecturalevangelist.com/building-information-modeling/4d-bim-modeling-improve-cost-scheduling-and-coordination-of-building-project-2.html |title=4D BIM Modeling: Improve Cost, Scheduling and Coordination of Building Project |publisher=architecturalevangelist.com |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230141135/http://www.architecturalevangelist.com/building-information-modeling/4d-bim-modeling-improve-cost-scheduling-and-coordination-of-building-project-2.html As an advanced construction management technique, it has been used by project delivery teams working on larger projects.<ref name=4DBIM-R-06>{{Cite web |url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:nHL2zKVJCHAJ:citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi%3D10.1.1.110.494%26rep%3Drep1%26type%3Dpdf+&hl=en&gl=in&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEEShtbA4OZLNI-pDNhsIbxhfUBVxkIUOors35dmnKMsy6G_UI85V3x1NCGU6vFrH9nRO5afeTactdmLb2kfO7R_SXqsbvfaropmI-5dWTj6yQGK5kcKcAv-zy6_9Kowbj_BqYtdW7&sig=AHIEtbQWjmYdMfzrbmvzj6KzrI5TaWwJBQ&pli=1 |title=Trends of 4D CAD applications for construction planning by David Heesom and Lamine Mahdjoubi |publisher=psu.edu |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-date=9 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409084513/http://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache%3AnHL2zKVJCHAJ%3Aciteseerx.ist.psu.edu%2Fviewdoc%2Fdownload%3Fdoi%3D10.1.1.110.494&rep=rep1&type=pdf+&hl=en&gl=in&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEEShtbA4OZLNI-pDNhsIbxhfUBVxkIUOors35dmnKMsy6G_UI85V3x1NCGU6vFrH9nRO5afeTactdmLb2kfO7R_SXqsbvfaropmI-5dWTj6yQGK5kcKcAv-zy6_9Kowbj_BqYtdW7&sig=AHIEtbQWjmYdMfzrbmvzj6KzrI5TaWwJBQ&pli=1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-07>{{Cite web |url=http://www.engr.psu.edu/ae/cic/publications/Conference/Yerrapathruni_Messner_Baratta_Horman_Using_4D_CAD.pdf |title=Using 4D CAD and Immersive Virtual Environments to Improve Construction Planning by Sai Yerrapathruni, John I. Messner, Anthony J. Baratta and Michael J. Horman |publisher=psu.edu |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130626100912/http://www.engr.psu.edu/ae/cic/publications/Conference/Yerrapathruni_Messner_Baratta_Horman_Using_4D_CAD.pdf |archive-date=26 June 2013 }}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-08>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipedr.com/vol13/32-T00059.pdf |title=4D CAD Application Examples and Directions for Development in Civil Engineering Projects by Joong-Min Kwak, Gwang-Yeol Choi, Nam-Jin Park, Hwa-Jin Seo and Leen-Seok Kang |publisher=ipedr.com |access-date=29 May 2012 |archive-date=4 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704021545/http://www.ipedr.com/vol13/32-T00059.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> 4D BIM has traditionally been used for higher end projects due to the associated costs, but technologies are now emerging that allow the process to be used by laymen or to drive processes such as manufacture.<ref name=4DBIM-R-10>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vicosoftware.com/what-is-4D-BIM/tabid/88206/Default.aspx|title=4D BIM from Vico website|publisher=vicosoftware.com|access-date=29 May 2012|archive-date=10 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610030131/http://www.vicosoftware.com/what-is-4D-BIM/tabid/88206/Default.aspx}}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-11>{{Cite web|url=http://ci-asce.org/node/8548|title=Management Pracitices in Construction by Mohammad kasirossafar|publisher=ci-asce.org|access-date=29 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616204600/http://ci-asce.org/node/8548|archive-date=16 June 2013}}</ref><ref name=4DBIM-R-12>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TcG1yCK5fewC|title= 4d CAD and Visualization in Construction: Developments and Applications by Raja R.
